title: The child who did not wake

plan.english: Little son, why did you not wake? In the evening you drank milk from my breast. Then at dawn you were cold. Hunger took you, and it did not take me. I weep indeed, and your father weeps. Lie, my son, in the cold.

plan.english: Long was the winter, and long was the hunger. Then the nights were cold. The grain vanished, and the cattle perished in the stalls. We devoured the bark of the trees, we ate the dogs. The old men walked out into the frost, they did not return home. Who will praise the old men? We, the living, shall praise them.

clauses.english: Long was the winter, and long was the hunger.
Then the nights were cold.
The grain vanished, and the cattle perished in the stalls.

The old men walked out into the frost, they did not return home.
Who will praise the old men?
We, the living, shall praise them.

plan.english: Then the plague came into the house, and it carried off my husband. It seized my daughter too. I am a widow, and I sit at the hearth. No one speaks inside the house. Heavenly ones, why then did you take them and leave me?

clauses.english: Then the plague came into the house, and it carried off my husband.
It seized my daughter too.
I am a widow, and I sit at the hearth.
No one speaks inside the house.
Heavenly ones, why then did you take them and leave me?

plan.english: Good cows, you lie in the field. Now I milked you early in the morning. Then the sickness arrived in the evening. In the night you were dead. The herd is gone, hunger has seized the young. What then will my boys eat in the winter?

clauses.english: Good cows, you lie in the field.
Now I milked you early in the morning.

In the night you were dead.
The herd is gone, hunger has seized the young.
What then will my boys eat in the winter?

plan.english: In that winter the snow fell early. The herds did not find grass, and the oxen perished in the stalls. Then the people devoured their flesh. The grain vanished from the pots. Then hunger arrived in the village. The young ones wept in the nights, and the mothers gave them nothing. Then the summer arrived, and few sheep were alive.

The herds did not find grass, and the oxen perished in the stalls.
Then the people devoured their flesh.
The grain vanished from the pots.
Then hunger arrived in the village.
The young ones wept in the nights, and the mothers gave them nothing.
Then the summer arrived, and few sheep were alive.

title: The old woman and the cold

plan.english: There was an old woman. In the hunger she spoke to her son. Lead me out into the cold, son. I eat, and I do not work. He wept, and he led her away in the night. She sat down under a tree, and she did not speak. In the morning he returned. She was cold, and she did not breathe. But her grandsons were alive.

clauses.english: There was an old woman.
In the hunger she spoke to her son.
Lead me out into the cold, son.
I eat, and I do not work.
He wept, and he led her away in the night.
She sat down under a tree, and she did not speak.
In the morning he returned.
She was cold, and she did not breathe.
But her grandsons were alive.

plan.english: The villagers waited for the spring. The snow lay on the hills, and the ice lay flat on the river. The calves perished. Then the dogs died. A young herdsman climbed up to the hills, and he was seeking roots. He did not return home. Then the sun became warm, and the ice was melting. The grass grew, and no beast devoured it. The spring came, and few people were alive.

clauses.english: The villagers waited for the spring.
The snow lay on the hills, and the ice lay flat on the river.
The calves perished.
Then the dogs died.
A young herdsman climbed up to the hills, and he was seeking roots.
He did not return home.
Then the sun became warm, and the ice was melting.
The grass grew, and no beast devoured it.
The spring came, and few people were alive.

plan.english: A stranger arrived in the village in the evening. The villagers gave him food and a bed. At dawn he went away. But the plague remained under that roof. The boys were coughing. Then the mother burned with heat. From that roof it went through the village. Many perished, and the living fled to the hills. Now the villagers fear strangers.

clauses.english: A stranger arrived in the village in the evening.
The villagers gave him food and a bed.

But the plague remained under that roof.
The boys were coughing.
Then the mother burned with heat.
From that roof it went through the village.
Many perished, and the living fled to the hills.
Now the villagers fear strangers.

plan.english: A shepherd had a hundred sheep. In one winter a sickness arrived among them. They coughed, and they lay down, and they did not stand up. The shepherd burned the dead ones in a great fire. Ten sheep remained. He drove them to the mountain. In the summer there were lambs. The shepherd praised the immortals.

title: The wise woman and the worm

plan.english: A boy was lying in sickness, and his belly was swelling. His mother brought a wise old woman. She looked at him, and she spoke. A worm dwells inside him. For nine nights she chanted the song. Then the worm came forth from his mouth. She ground it with a stone, and she threw it into the fire. The boy woke up and drank milk. The mother gave the wise one a goat.

plan.english: In one summer it did not rain. The rivers dried up, and the grass became dry. The cattle stood at the spring, and they did not find water. The king led the villagers to the assembly. They took counsel. Let us give the greatest bull to Perkʷunos. They slew the bull on the stone, and the smoke arose to the sky. Then Perkʷunos thundered, and it rained. The people rejoiced.

plan.english: In the hunger the elders were sitting in the assembly. One said: Feed the warriors, and they will protect us. Another said: May the children eat. They are our offspring. The oldest woman stood up, and she spoke. We old ones have seen many winters. Feed the young ones. They were silent, and they did so.
